newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Agip reports three new gas finds off Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Agip reports three new gas finds off Egypt.

text.p: Italy's Agip announced three new gas finds in the offshore basin of the Nile Delta on Wednesday in a statement that showed the wells had a combined maximum daily productive capacity of 1.64 million cubic metres.

The company, a unit of state energy concern ENI, said two of the finds were in the El Temsah concession where Agip is an equal partner in an exploratory joint venture with Amoco Egypt Oil Co, a unit of Amoco Corp.
"According to initial estimates, the two discoveries increase the offshore reserves of the basin of the Nile Delta by more than 28 billion cubic metres of gas," the statement said.
The third find was in the West Abu Madi area where Agip has a 50 percent share in a three-way venture with Amoco Egypt Oil Co and Marathon Petroleum Nile Delta Ltd.

Agip said one of the El Temsah finds was at the Karous 1 well in the central area of the concession 40 km north/northwest of Port Said where gas had been found at a depth of about 1,300 metres showing an estimated daily maximum output of 450,000 cubic metres.

The second well, Tuna 1, was in the northern part of the concession 70 km north/northwest of Port Said. Gas was found at about 1,100 metres showing a daily maximum output of 340,000 cubic metres a day.
Agip said the West Abu Madi find was in the Nidoco 9 well, about three km off the town of Batim in the Mediterranean.
It said gas condensate had been found at a depth of 3,400 metres.
"It is estimated that the productive capacity of the well may reach around 850,000 cubic metres of gas and 500 barrels of gas condensate a day," the statement said.
